summary.headline: Castrol India Q3 CY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 1,735 crore, but EBITDA fell 19% to INR 262 crore (~15% margin) on raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Q3 revenue from operations was INR 1,735 crore, up 27% YoY but down 7% QoQ, while EBITDA fell 19% YoY to INR 262 crore and PAT fell 23% YoY to INR 176 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to a sharp rise in commodity and raw material costs (cited as a 60-plus percent increase in the raw material bill) and adverse currency moves, partly offset by early-year pricing actions. Over nine months, revenue grew 20% to INR 5,151 crore, EBITDA rose 11% to INR 1,086 crore and PAT rose 9% to INR 766 crore. Management declined to give forward quarterly guidance and said margins will sit outside the 21-24% EBITDA band in the short to medium term.

segments.name: Industrial lubricants
segments.commentary: Delivered another quarter of double-digit volume growth in the September quarter; added close to 400 customers net over the full year and 9 months, with growth in steel and cement and new metalworking fluid launches (Hysol 35 XBB, Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free). Management said industrial margin is healthy and above last year's level.

segments.name: Automotive / consumer and commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: No separate volume figures given. Management said Q2 and Q3 were managed together and volume growth looked healthy; company claims market share held across categories. Institutional customers include Tata, Maruti and JCB.

segments.name: Thermal management / data-centre cooling
segments.commentary: Early-stage. Two latest products certified by NVIDIA about 1.5 months before the call for direct-to-chip cooling; business is in ongoing pilots and not a substantial part of revenue or profit today.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance given; management cited unprecedented raw material volatility.
Medium-term EBITDA margin expected to fall outside the 21-24% band in the short to medium term; the 21-24% band remains the target over time.
Management said it will operate within a 21-24% EBITDA frame over the medium term while growing volume at least 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate.
Plant utilisation expected to stay in the 70-80% range through the year.
Market growth in India estimated at 3-4% in a normal year; this year may see headwinds, with Castrol tracking ahead.
Capex historically INR 100-150 crore per year, focused on plant innovation, capacity and consumer/trade visibility.

Stonepeak acquisition of Castrol from BP: completion targeted by end CY26 per the deal; management said licence work across 50+ countries is progressing well, with SEBI disclosure to follow on completion.
capex_capacity: Plants run at around 70-80% utilisation; expected to remain in the same range through the year, with seasonal flex.
Historical capex of INR 100-150 crore per year; no specific CY27 capex figure given.
Localisation of inputs and reformulation are being used to reduce bill of materials and cash cost.
Supply-chain efficiency work under way for 6-7 months to partly offset raw material inflation.
demand_pricing: Raw material bill up 60-plus percent in Q3; COGS as a percentage of sales up 61% YoY.
Pricing actions taken early in the year; further pricing to be taken as and when required, calibrated by sector, with no forward guidance.
About 40% of business is B2B; some B2B contracts have price-flex clauses for input-cost pass-through, while B2C pricing varies by channel.
Base oil prices: Base Oil 2 down about 5% and Base Oil 3 down about 7% in Q3 per an analyst; management said the cost environment remains substantially challenged versus last year.
Crude oil went from about $120 in Q2 to about $80, and is now back at $114-115 per management.

Network of about 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 in rural small-town India; Auto Care in 50,000 stores; about 870 Castrol Auto Service centres, 37,000 independent bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops; Rural Service Express at over 1,000 locations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume guidance and how is pricing balanced against market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance for the next few months given the unprecedented raw material moves; it reiterated the aim to gain volume and share, with pricing balanced to let consumers move to new price points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and margin guidance for CY27, and hedging plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex historically INR 100-150 crore; investments prioritise growth drivers. Margin protection is to come from a mix of pricing and cost prudence; no hedging detail was given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Stonepeak acquisition and the DPS filing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence work across more than 50 countries is progressing well; SEBI will be informed on completion, with no timeline beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is Castrol refocusing on the OEM business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not call out OEM as a separate focus; it said it works with OEMs such as Tata, Maruti and JCB on new engine platform technology.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise sales and Q3 volume trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth ahead of market over nine months; industrial grew double digits in Q3; automotive volumes were described as healthy across Q2 and Q3 combined, with no specific figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reference margin per litre, and does lower absolute EBITDA imply lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-litre EBITDA is an internal frame, and the external measure is percentage margin: 26% in Q2, 15% in Q3, 21% over six and nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Are plants and margins expected to recover, and what levers are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 21-24% band will be reached only once volatility subsides, with levers in supplier diversification, localisation, reformulation and supply-chain efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre cooling: size of opportunity and how sales are routed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said products are globally approved and sold through Castrol India, with NVIDIA certification as a base requirement; it declined to size the opportunity, saying it is not yet material.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude/FX volatility: margin per litre is the stated measure, but guidance has been withdrawn.
Q4 CY26 margin and volume recovery; watch pricing action and base oil rebates in Oct-Dec.
Volume softness in the short to medium term given market headwinds.
Stonepeak-BP transaction: completion by end CY26 and any change to the timeline.
Limited disclosure: analysts pressed for segment and volume detail, and an analyst asked for more specific guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the industrial and rural growth engines, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and guidance, citing raw material and currency volatility. Management was evasive on volume split, data-centre sizing and the timeline for the Stonepeak deal.
key_quotes: We are not giving a guidance for the next few months because it's unprecedented in terms of the raw material price movement, right?
For us, margin per liter is a true measure. And on that basis, we have fully absorbed cost inflation.
We will hold ourselves to the frame of operating the business at 21% to 24% EBITDA.

growth.why: Management withdrew quarterly guidance citing unprecedented raw-material volatility, expects EBITDA margin outside the 21-24% band in the short-to-medium term and says volumes may stay soft, while still targeting volume growth at 1.5-2x market (3-4%) with plant utilisation at 70-80% and no new capacity additions quantified.
